title: Master Control Handle and Eight Detents
summary: Understand the configured EB, B3, B2, B1, N, P1, P2 and P3 control positions.
objectives: Explain traction, neutral and service braking
Distinguish emergency braking from routine braking

sections.heading: Power positions: P1, P2, P3
sections.body: The three power positions request increasing levels of traction effort in this training configuration. Speed will change over time depending on traction, resistance, train load and operating conditions.
points: P1 is a low power request.
P2 is a greater power request.
P3 is the highest configured power request.

sections.heading: Neutral: N
sections.body: Neutral requests no powered traction and no active service-brake step from the combined controller. If a train is moving, it can continue rolling while resistive forces gradually affect speed; N does not mean an immediate stop.

sections.heading: Service braking: B1, B2, B3
sections.body: The three service-braking detents request graduated braking. B1 is the lowest, B2 is intermediate and B3 is the greatest configured service-brake request. The actual relationship between controller position and braking force depends on rolling stock design.

sections.heading: Emergency: EB
sections.body: EB is the emergency-brake detent in this teaching arrangement. It is reserved for emergency response, not routine speed regulation. A separate emergency-brake switch may initiate the same emergency-braking state.

sections.heading: Interpret the controller safely
sections.body: A controller position is a request, not a measurement. Use the speedometer and relevant brake indications to observe its effect. On real trains, operating technique and recovery procedures are vehicle-specific.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the purpose of N?
choices: Coasting / neither service braking nor traction from the handle
reviewQuestions.explanation: N is the neutral position of the configured combined handle.

reviewQuestions.question: Which is the highest configured service braking detent?
reviewQuestions.explanation: B3 requests the greatest configured service braking of the three service detents.

reviewQuestions.question: What does EB represent?
reviewQuestions.explanation: EB is the emergency-brake detent, separate from regular service-braking steps.
